The django-mojo side of the fleet code deploy (#1458, done) is live: webhook
receiver, canary orchestration, `migrate_locked`, `sanity_check`,
`deploy_status`. **It is inert until this repo speaks its contract** — today
`update.sh` deploys `origin/main` instead of a pinned commit, reports nothing,
and `post_deploy.sh` upgrades django-mojo unpinned and gates migrations on a
flag file that cannot serialise anything.

Scoping found the item is substantially bigger than the two scripts:

- **The skeleton already has a competing trigger plane.**
  `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` curls `POST /api/system/update` on every
  push, broadcasting `update.sh` to every node simultaneously — no canary, no
  pinning, no lock. Both systems live means every push runs two interleaved
  fleet deploys. This item retires the legacy plane and defines the one-shot
  cutover.
- **The feature's apps are not installed here.** `apps/apps.json` carries
  neither `mojo.apps.edge` nor `mojo.apps.github`, so as filed the webhook
  would 404 forever and every `manage.py deploy_status` call would be an
  unknown command. Installing them is part of this item. The framework-side
  prerequisites that surfaced (the `EDGE_CONVERGE_ENABLED` cron gate and one
  contract-doc correction) are **already merged** to django-mojo `main` as
  #1575 (`39c2e896`); what remains is **publishing the django-mojo release**
  that carries them — the cutover's first step.

The authoritative node contract is django-mojo
`docs/django_developer/edge/deploy.md` ("Required skeleton changes") — kept
current there, not here.

- **Project**: django-mojo-skeleton (maestro project 50; repo

### Requirements

- `apps/apps.json`: add `mojo.apps.edge` + `mojo.apps.github`, remove
  `system`; their migrations (edge 0001/0002, github 0001) applied once at
  cutover.
- `aws/update.sh` speaks the deploy argv (`--sha`, `--framework`,
  `--migrate`), waits on an `flock`, short-circuits on target, reports
  terminal status through `manage.py deploy_status`, and keeps
  `bin/jobman stop` last (output-redirected — see D4).
- `aws/post_deploy.sh` installs the **pinned** framework version and runs

- The legacy trigger plane is removed: `apps/system`, the deploy workflow,
  `aws/post_update.sh`, and the `SYSTEM_UPDATE_TOKEN` machinery throughout

- Node provisioning gains `EDGE_DEPLOY_SCRIPT`/`EDGE_DEPLOY_BRANCH`
  (prod-profile settings) and `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (generated at
  deploy.py config-init, persisted to `var/deploy.json`, written into the
  S3-published `var/django.conf` — any node behind the LB may serve the
  webhook).
- A documented cutover checklist moves a running fleet from old to new.

## Plan

Scoped 2026-08-08 from the django-mojo session that built #1458, with full
read access to this repo; the build must run in a skeleton checkout.
Red-teamed; 15 objections, 4 blocking, all dispositioned — see Challenge.

**Build routing**: inline, session model.

### Objective

A push to `main` deploys through #1458's canary flow and **only** through it:
the deploy apps are installed, `update.sh` performs one pinned, locked,
status-reporting update per box, the legacy broadcast plane no longer exists,
and a documented cutover moves a running fleet onto the new flow.

### Decisions resolved in scoping

#### D1 — install the deploy apps; retire the legacy plane; one trigger system

`apps/apps.json` (the skeleton's INSTALLED_APPS registry — built by
`paths.configure_apps`; **not** `config/settings/`) gains `mojo.apps.edge`
and `mojo.apps.github` and loses `system`. That is what mounts
`/api/github/deploy/webhook` and `/api/edge/deploy` (django-mojo's URL map
iterates INSTALLED_APPS) and what lets Django discover
`deploy_status`/`migrate_locked`/`sanity_check`. Their migrations (edge
0001/0002, github 0001) apply once at cutover (D7).

Deleted: `apps/system/` (the app is *only* the update trigger),
`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (the push webhook replaces CI's deploy step
natively; workflows run from the pushed commit, so the deleted file cannot
double-fire), `aws/post_update.sh` (uninvoked legacy residue), and the
`SYSTEM_UPDATE_TOKEN` machinery through **all** of `aws/deploy.py` —
config-init/globals, `write_django_conf`, the `github-secret` step, docstring
— not just the step body.

Rejected: keeping `/api/system/update` as an emergency all-nodes hammer. Two
trigger planes is the "deploys must not overlap" violation #1458 closed; the
sanctioned override is `POST /api/edge/deploy` (global `manage_deploy`,
canaried), and the hands-on escape hatch is D2's `--manual`.

Installing `mojo.apps.edge` would also schedule its `converge_edge` cron
(cron discovery imports `cronjobs` for every installed app), broadcasting
nginx convergence onto an `edge` channel no skeleton runner consumes — Job
rows piling up every 10 minutes against tables this deployment doesn't use.
**The skeleton must not adopt the vhost plane to get the deploy plane**, so
#1575 (D8, landed) gated that cron behind `EDGE_CONVERGE_ENABLED`
(get_static, default True) and this repo sets it `False` in prod settings.

#### D2 — `update.sh` modes: deploy argv, `--manual`, and bare-is-an-error

- **Deploy mode** — `--sha <7-40 hex> --framework <version> [--migrate]`:
  what `deploy_node` invokes. Fetch, `git reset --hard <sha>` (never
  `origin/main`), pinned install, optional locked migration, status report.
- **`--manual`** — the old hands-on behavior for one box (`origin/main`,
  latest framework, no migration, **no status writes**), under a
  non-blocking flock (`-n`: an operator at a prompt gets an immediate
  "in flight" answer).
- **Bare invocation is a usage error** (exit 2) naming both modes.
  Muscle-memory `bash aws/update.sh` mid-deploy must not race the fleet with
  untracked state. Verified: nothing else in the repo invokes it bare — the
  only callers are the deleted plane and the rewritten docs.

Argument validation mirrors django-mojo's: sha `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$`, not
all-zero; version `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._!+-]{0,63}$`. Defense in depth —
the values already crossed `deploy_node`'s validation.

`PROJ_PATH="${PROJ_PATH:-/opt/api}"` + `cd "$PROJ_PATH"` replace the
hard-coded pwd check — the test seam, and the script stops depending on the
engine's inherited cwd.

#### D3 — flock **waits** in deploy mode; short-circuit by prefix

`exec 9>>var/update.lock`. Deploy mode: `flock -w 600 9 || exit 1` — a
chained deploy (a push that landed mid-canary-rollback) queues behind the
rollback instead of either interleaving or false-failing; timeout → non-zero
→ the still-alive `deploy_node` files an accurate incident. `--manual`:
`flock -n 9` (fail fast at the prompt). Exit on flock failure is **non-zero**
in deploy mode on purpose: a same-box conflict is real contention, not a
benign ghost — ghosts are handled by the short-circuit and by django-mojo's
NX/CAS layer.

Short-circuit (deploy mode, after the lock): `git rev-parse HEAD` **starts
with** `--sha` (the manual endpoint accepts abbreviated shas; strict equality
would never match them) *and* `python3 -c "import mojo; print(mojo.__version__)"`
equals `--framework` → log, exit 0. Sha alone is not enough — a
framework-only re-pin must still run.

#### D4 — the `--migrate` run reports **before** it rolls back

1. Capture rollback state first: `var/previous_sha` (`git rev-parse HEAD`)
   and `var/previous_framework` (`mojo.__version__`), before any fetch.
2. Install: reset to `--sha`, `sudo bash aws/post_deploy.sh --framework <v>
   --migrate` (pinned pip, `migrate_locked --noinput`, collectstatic, nginx,
   restart, probe).
3. Verify: `python3 bin/manage.py sanity_check`.
4. **On any failure from 2-3:**
   `deploy_status set failed --sha <sha> --detail "<step>"` **first**, *then*
   roll back — reset to `previous_sha`,
   `sudo bash aws/post_deploy.sh --framework <previous_framework>` (no
   migrate; migrations are deliberately not rolled back, per #1458), then
   `sanity_check`. **The report precedes the rollback because the rollback
   may reinstall a framework that predates `deploy_status`** — report while
   the reporting tool is guaranteed to exist. A rollback that itself fails
   best-effort re-reports with `--detail "rollback failed"`, tolerating both
   exit 3 and command absence (`|| true`, logged).
5. On success: `deploy_status set deploying --sha <sha>` (exit 3 tolerated —
   superseded is not a failure), write `var/version`, then
   `./bin/jobman stop >> var/update.log 2>&1` **last**. The redirect is
   load-bearing: `deploy_node` runs this script with `capture_output` pipes
   whose read end dies with the engine — jobman's own echo after killing the
   engine would SIGPIPE the jobman script between "stop engine" and "stop
   scheduler", leaving the scheduler alive on old code. Only this one line is
   redirected; everything earlier stays on stdout/stderr so `deploy_node`'s
   failure incidents keep their output tail.

Fleet-node runs (no `--migrate`) neither report nor roll back: a failure
exits non-zero *before* `jobman stop`, so the still-alive `deploy_node` job
files the incident — built and tested in #1458.

#### D5 — `post_deploy.sh`: two flags, no flag file, bare stays valid

`--framework <version>` → `pip install django-mojo==<version>`; absent →
today's `pip install --upgrade django-mojo`. `--migrate` →
`python3 bin/manage.py migrate_locked --noinput`; absent → no migration. The
`var/allow_migrate` block (`:48-63`) is deleted — the advisory lock inside
`migrate_locked` is the serialisation the flag file's own comment says it was
a placeholder for.

**Bare `post_deploy.sh` remaining valid is cutover-load-bearing, not a
convenience**: the final legacy broadcast executes the OLD `update.sh` (bash
holds the old inode through the git reset), whose line 14 invokes the NEW
`post_deploy.sh` with no arguments. The harness pins this with its own test.

Test seams, prod-identical defaults: `NGINX_ETC="${NGINX_ETC:-/etc/nginx}"`,
`SYSTEMD_ETC="${SYSTEMD_ETC:-/etc/systemd/system}"`.

#### D6 — settings placement and the secret's supply chain

- `config/settings/prod/__init__.py` (flat assignments, matching its idiom):
  `EDGE_DEPLOY_SCRIPT = ["/opt/api/aws/update.sh"]`,
  `EDGE_DEPLOY_BRANCH = "main"`, `EDGE_CONVERGE_ENABLED = False` (D8's
  gate). **Prod profile only, not defaults/** — django-mojo ships no
  `EDGE_DEPLOY_SCRIPT` default *on purpose* (an unconfigured box must refuse
  to run a deploy), and a defaults-level value would arm every dev/test
  checkout of every project built on this skeleton. Prod-only preserves that
  posture while making real nodes work out of the box.
  **No `sudo` wrapper in the argv**: the engine runs as `ec2-user`
  (`/etc/cron.d/3_mojo_jobs`), which owns the clone; a root-run script would
  root-own `.git` objects and break every later ec2-user git operation.
  `update.sh` itself sudos `post_deploy.sh`, exactly as today.
- `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`: generated at `aws/deploy.py` config-init (beside
  the other generated credentials), persisted in `var/deploy.json`, written
  by `write_django_conf` so the **cache step's** S3 publish distributes it
  fleet-wide — the sequencing matters because settings load at process
  start, and the webhook 403s until every node has it. The old
  `github-secret` step becomes `github-webhook`: create the push webhook
  (`/api/github/deploy/webhook`, `application/json`, that secret) via `gh
  api`, with the repo's existing printed-manual-fallback pattern.

#### D7 — the cutover: publish, provision, one last legacy broadcast

A numbered checklist in `updating.md`; order is the content:

1. **Publish the django-mojo release** carrying the deploy plane and #1575's
   gate (`publish.py`, operator-run). The cutover's own
   `pip install --upgrade` is what installs it — before that release exists,
   the new scripts land on a framework with no deploy plane.
2. Put `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in the S3 `django.conf` (deploy.py cache
   step) and create the webhook (github-webhook step). Before cutover it
   collects harmless 404s.
3. Merge this item to `main`. No workflow fires (deleted with the merge).
4. **One manual legacy trigger**: `curl -X POST /api/system/update` with the
   old token — the running nodes still serve the old endpoint and handler,
   so every node takes one final legacy-style update that lands the new
   scripts, the new framework, the installed apps, and removes the old plane
   from the deployed tree.
5. **Apply the new apps' migrations once**: on any one node,
   `python3 bin/manage.py migrate_locked --noinput` (edge 0001/0002, github
   0001). Until then the new tables don't exist; the gated converge cron is
   off (D6), so nothing touches them in the gap.
6. Restart engines' world knowledge: nothing to do — cron `jobman start`
   already brought engines back on the new code.
7. **Re-bake the golden AMI** (`aws/deploy.py bake-ami`): a node booted from
   the old AMI has no `EDGE_DEPLOY_SCRIPT` in its baked settings and would
   refuse deploys forever — under the old flow stale AMIs self-healed via
   the broadcast; under the new flow the AMI must start current.
8. From then on: pushes deploy via the webhook; hands-on fixes via
   `update.sh --manual`; fleet-wide manual deploys via
   `POST /api/edge/deploy`.

A node down during step 4 misses the cutover: it keeps serving old code and
takes no deploys (visible in the orchestrator's runner snapshot, not
silently divergent); bring it over with `--manual` or terminate it — the
re-baked AMI covers replacements.

#### D8 — the framework-side prerequisites (landed as #1575; release pending)

Three framework-side pieces this plan depends on, none of which this repo may
make (workspec: "kept current there, not here"). The first two are **done** —
django-mojo #1575, commit `39c2e896`, verified by `test_edge` (170/170):

1. `converge_edge` gated behind `EDGE_CONVERGE_ENABLED`
   (`settings.get_static`, default `True` — zero behavior change for
   existing edge users; D6 sets it `False` here).
2. `deploy.md`'s rollback sentence corrected to report-then-rollback (D4's
   ordering, with its reason) — the contract doc and this plan now agree.
3. **Still open: publish the django-mojo release** (the version D7 step 1
   installs) — operator-run `publish.py`.

### Edge cases and error handling

- **Ghost redelivery / duplicate publish** → short-circuit exits 0; a
  *concurrent* duplicate waits on the lock, then short-circuits.
- **Chained deploy racing the canary's rollback** → waits on `flock -w`,
  runs after the rollback completes; timeout → non-zero → accurate incident.
- **`deploy_status` exits 3 (superseded)** → tolerated at every call site.
- **Rollback reinstalls a pre-`deploy_status` framework** → the failure was
  already reported (D4's ordering); the post-rollback re-report is
  best-effort `|| true`.
- **`--manual` during a live deploy** → `-n` flock refuses immediately.
- **Fleet node fails mid-run** → non-zero exit before `jobman stop`;
  `deploy_node` files the incident. Non-migrate runs never write status.
- **Node down during the cutover broadcast** → serves old code, takes no
  deploys, visible in the runner snapshot; `--manual` or replace-from-AMI.
- **`var/update.lock` staleness** → none; flock dies with the fd, and `var/`
  is gitignored so `git clean -fd` cannot unlink it mid-run.

### Testing plan

Two self-asserting bash harnesses (no bats), each building a temp
`PROJ_PATH` with a stub `bin/` on `PATH` (`git`, `pip`, `python3`, `sudo`,
`curl`, `nginx`, `systemctl`, `bin/jobman`, `bin/manage.py` — every argv
recorded, exit codes scriptable):

`tests/deploy/test_update_sh.sh`:

| Property | How |
|---|---|
| bare invocation exits 2, nothing executed | empty stub log |
| bad sha / zero sha / bad version refused before any action | exit ≠ 0, empty log |
| short-circuit: HEAD prefix-matches sha + version matches → exit 0, no fetch | log has only the two probes |
| deploy-mode flock waits (slow first run, second queues then runs); `--manual` `-n` fails fast | background run + sleep stub |
| canary failure: `deploy_status set failed` BEFORE the rollback `git reset` | log order |
| rollback resets to previous_sha, reinstalls previous framework, no `--migrate` | `post_deploy.sh` argv in log |
| success order: `post_deploy.sh --framework X --migrate` → `sanity_check` → `deploy_status set deploying` → `jobman stop` last | log order |
| fleet run (no `--migrate`): zero `deploy_status` calls; failure exits non-zero before `jobman stop` | log |
| `--manual`: bare `post_deploy.sh`, no status calls | log argv |
| `deploy_status` exit 3 does not fail the run | stub exit 3 |

`tests/deploy/test_post_deploy_sh.sh` (with `NGINX_ETC`/`SYSTEMD_ETC`
pointed into the temp dir):

| Property | How |
|---|---|
| `--framework X` → `pip install django-mojo==X`; bare → `--upgrade` | log argv |
| `--migrate` → `migrate_locked --noinput`; absent → no migrate call at all | log |
| **bare invocation completes the legacy sequence** (cutover-load-bearing, D5) | full run, exit 0 |
| failure in any step aborts before the restart (die-loudly preserved) | stub exit ≠ 0 |

Riders: `bash -n` on both scripts; `shellcheck` advisory when present.

Out of honest reach, stated plainly: a real fleet deploy, real webhook
delivery, and the cutover itself — argued on a staging fleet of ≥2 nodes
(canary ≠ orchestrator), per #1458's same boundary.

file:line verified before disposition. The four blocking ones reshaped the
